figures.data: Defect signature: small holes/cavities in the bead. Causes/fixes: 1) Dirty workpiece or fill material — clean to bare metal, keep fill material and electrode free of oil, coatings, residues; 2) Inconsistent welding speed — maintain steady weld speed.

figures.data: Defect signature: meandering/snaking bead centerline. Causes/fixes: 1) Inaccurate welding — use two hands or rest hand on steady surface; 2) Inconsistent welding speed — maintain steady weld speed.
figures.description: TOP VIEW of a stick weld bead whose overlapping crescent ripples wander side to side instead of following a straight line, ending in a rounded molten ball.
figures.label: Stick Weld – Crooked/Wavy Bead

figures.data: Fine spatter is normal; grainy and large spatter is a problem. Cause/fix: Dirty workpiece or fill material — clean workpiece down to bare metal; keep fill material and Electrode clean and free from oil, coatings, and other residues.
figures.description: TOP VIEW of a stick weld bead surrounded by numerous coarse, dark, irregular metal droplets scattered on the base metal on both sides of and along the bead.
figures.label: Stick Weld – Excessive Spatter

figures.data: Defect signature: hole melted through base material. Causes/fixes: 1) Workpiece overheating — reduce current; 2) Welding speed too slow — increase welding speed and keep it steady; 3) Excessive material at weld — reduce amount of fill material.
figures.description: TOP VIEW of a stick weld bead where the center has melted completely away, leaving a large open white void hole through the base material ringed by melted metal, with the molten ball at the right end.
